title: Inspiration of Scripture
definition: The Inspiration of Scripture means God breathed out His Word through human authors so that Scripture is truly God’s Word and fully trustworthy.
summary: The Inspiration of Scripture means God breathed out His Word through human authors so that Scripture is truly God’s Word and fully trustworthy.
christFocus: Jesus treated the written Scriptures as God’s own Word, and the Scriptures inspired by the Holy Spirit bear witness to Christ, His Gospel, and His kingdom.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture is inspired because God is its ultimate author. The Holy Spirit worked through real people, in real history, using their words and situations, while ensuring that what was written was the Word God intended His people to receive.

Inspiration does not make the Bible less human or less understandable. It means the Bible is more than human. Through Scripture, God speaks truly, faithfully, and with authority. The believer can come to the Word with confidence because God has not given a confused or unreliable witness.

The same Spirit who inspired Scripture points us to Christ through Scripture. The written Word reveals the living Word. Inspiration matters because the Gospel is not built on human memory, religious imagination, or tradition alone, but on the God-breathed witness that reveals Jesus Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
A believer who doubts whether God has spoken will struggle to stand firm when life is painful or confusing. Inspiration assures the weary, the new believer, the teacher, and the recovering person that Scripture is not merely advice from the past but God’s living Word for His people.

This doctrine also protects the Church from placing human voices above God’s voice. Teachers, pastors, counselors, and study tools can help, but none of them breathe out truth the way God has in Scripture.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Approach the Bible with reverence and expectation. Ask the Holy Spirit to help you receive what He inspired, test every teaching by Scripture, and let the God-breathed Word shape your worship, convictions, and obedience to Christ.
